qualification_scope: Windows SDK callback controllers with injected WinFsp lifecycle operations. The AMD work used the actual installed runtime and adapter on the physical Windows host. Volumes were disposable memory images.

tests.scope: Final controller logic. Later live-fixture dimensions are compiled only in the HIP fixture build.

retained_failures.outcome: Intermediate build requested a nonexistent worker-exchange target. The corrected invocation built the repository's actual target.

A 13-file installed callback fixture returned before publication at its 57-second deadline. The four-dispatch reply verified, all initial bytes reopened on CPU and the worker retired. The final fixture requests the smallest group with four admitted dispatches and has an 85-second publication deadline.

pilot_comparison.method: Eight pairs per cohort on the same application, worker, runtime and input bytes. The pairing alternated serial-first and queued-first with both cohort orders. The pilot could reduce the requested queue depth of four to two for shorter transfers. Each trial verified one actual worker and reopened every file independently on CPU.
pilot_comparison.timing: Complete time sums discovery, maintenance and verified compaction. Scheduling opportunities in these comparisons are modeled, while runtime execution, memory admission and timing use the physical host. The paired interval is a percentile bootstrap of median queued-minus-serial differences over 20,000 fixed-seed draws. At eight pairs the nearest-rank p95 equals the observed maximum.
pilot_comparison.conclusion: Both paired complete-time intervals include zero. Every pair preserved image size and selected member count. The final policy requires a full wait group at the approved depth and uses serial waits below that geometry.
